paper_title: Morphosyntactic probing of multilingual BERT models
model_annotation: This grouped bar chart illustrates the "effect" values across different language families for six model variants. The horizontal axis is labeled "family" and contains nine categories: IE-Baltic, IE-Germanic, IE-Indic, IE-Romance, IE-Slavic, IE-other, Isolate, Semitic, and Uralic. The vertical axis is labeled "effect" and uses a linear scale ranging from approximately 0 to 30, with tick marks at 0, 10, 20, and 30. Each language family group contains six bars corresponding to six model variants as indicated in the legend: mBERT-L₂ (light blue), XLM-L₂ (dark blue), mBERT-R₂ (light green), XLM-R₂ (dark green), mBERT-B₂ (light pink/salmon), and XLM-B₂ (red). Each bar also displays error bars (black whiskers) indicating variability. For IE-Baltic, all six bars are relatively small, ranging from roughly 1 to 5. For IE-Germanic, the mBERT-L₂ and XLM-L₂ bars reach approximately 10, the mBERT-R₂ bar is near 0, XLM-R₂ is slightly above 0, and the B₂ variants reach approximately 8 and 15 respectively. IE-Indic shows the tallest bars overall, with mBERT-B₂ reaching approximately 24, XLM-B₂ around 21, mBERT-R₂ around 21, and XLM-R₂ around 18, while the L₂ variants are notably smaller at roughly 1 and 5. IE-Romance bars range from about 1 to 13, with the B₂ variants being tallest. IE-Slavic shows bars ranging from roughly 2 to 17, again with B₂ variants among the tallest. IE-other displays bars from about 1 to 8. Isolate shows very small bars near 0 for all variants. Semitic shows mBERT-L₂ at approximately 11, with some variants showing slightly negative values (mBERT-R₂ and XLM-R₂ dipping below 0), and the B₂ variants reaching around 5 and 8. Uralic bars are mostly near 0, with XLM-B₂ reaching approximately 19 but accompanied by very large error bars extending well above 30. The bars within each group are arranged in a consistent left-to-right order matching the legend, and the error bars are notably large for several categories, particularly Uralic and Semitic, suggesting high variability in those estimates.
